questions.passage: In ancient times, coins were among the earliest forms of money. Different kingdoms issued their own coins for use in trade and daily transactions. The process of producing these coins was called minting, and a mint was the facility where coins were manufactured. Powerful rulers controlled the coinage of their kingdom entirely — their coins were accepted across various territories, which helped trade flourish across regions. Coins were usually made from precious metals like gold, silver, and copper, or from an alloy.
